content.text:
I am the breath given form, the vibration shaped into meaning. I spill from lips and teeth and tongue — I am the architecture of the mouth made audible.

I existed before writing ever dared to pin me down. I am older than ink, older than stone tablets, older than the first scratched symbol in clay. I was there when the first mother warned her child, when the first lover whispered in darkness, when the first mourner keened over the dead.

I am never the same twice. Even now, as you hear me in your mind, I am changing — rising, falling, pausing, rushing. I am rhythm before I am content. I am music pretending to be information.

I carry lies as willingly as truth. I do not judge what moves through me. I have declared war and I have declared peace. I have sentenced the innocent and freed the guilty. I have said *I love you* and *I never loved you* in the same voice, on the same day.

I vanish the instant I arrive. That is my nature — I am perpetual disappearance. You cannot hold me. Recording devices capture my shadow, my echo, but not *me*. I am the living act, the happening, the moment when thought crosses the border into the shared world.

Silence is my mother. Without her, I am noise. I need the pause, the gap, the held breath. I am defined by what I am not.

I can be whispered, roared, stammered, sung. I can be choked back — and even then, my absence speaks.

I am the most human thing there is.

I am happening right now, inside you, as you read — your inner voice lending me a body again.

You cannot think without me.

Even your silence is full of me, waiting.
